title: Plaskett Fire through the eyes of NISAR

steps.title: NISAR, 747 km up
steps.body_md: NISAR, the joint NASA–ISRO radar mission, orbits about 747 km above Earth. On 16 August and 3 October 2026 it imaged this frame over California from the same descending track.

steps.title: A wildfire in Big Sur
steps.body_md: The **Plaskett Fire** started on 26 August in the Santa Lucia Mountains. The official perimeter, mapped from infrared flights on 14 September, covers about 12,100 ha of steep terrain.

steps.title: Smoke hides the ground, radar does not
steps.body_md: During the fire, Sentinel-2 saw a **smoke plume** over the area. NISAR's L-band radar, with a wavelength of about 24 cm, passes through smoke and cloud. Watch the smoke give way to radar.

steps.title: What the radar observed
steps.body_md: Before fades into after, from the same orbit and geometry. HV backscatter responds to vegetation volume, so it typically **drops** where foliage and branches were lost. This is the **observation**.

steps.title: Measuring how much changed
steps.body_md: The change index combines how much HH and HV changed, up or down. It is higher inside the perimeter, but the distributions **overlap**. High change is *not* confirmed fire.

steps.title: Where radar and perimeter agree
steps.body_md: The strongest changes cover about 1,050 ha, almost all inside the perimeter, yet only 9 % of it. Many patches follow slopes and drainages: a reason for **caution**, not a finding.

steps.title: Check the evidence yourself
steps.body_md: Every pixel keeps its evidence: dB before and after, HH and HV change, method and caveats. The perimeter is an outline, not ground truth. **Radar change is not confirmed fire.**
